analysis:
All supplied units are documentation-only: CHANGELOG.md (head excerpts, historical release notes, lines 1414-2008) and docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (date bump plus a new 'Calibration ownership and foreground admission' section and a file-map row). No source, wire, key-custody, attestation, authorization or cache-crypto changes are in these units, so there is no security regression or new attack surface to report here.

What the docs describe, for the next pass to verify against code (not supplied): IdleCalibrationCoordinator (startIfIdle, beginForeground), EngineV2Bridge+ModelCalibrationRequests (runModelCalibrationRequest) and EngineV2Bridge+Events (runPump). The doc says: one calibration session per Mac; no raised memory/concurrency limits and no new capacity wire fields; a customer request takes a foreground lease, cancels calibration and waits for actual retirement before admission; calibration samples never increment served-request or output-token totals. Relevant threats: T-010 (cancellation propagation/DoS), T-029 (GPU occupancy), T-028/TB-007 (residual KV/GPU data; the doc explicitly says retirement does not mean the allocator returned bytes), T-041 (prefix cache). Open questions: whether calibration probes are synthetic and never touch the prefix cache or donate SSD blocks (T-041), whether any consumer prompt content is used, and whether a stuck probe can delay foreground admission beyond request deadlines. Doc states original deadlines and memory admission remain authoritative.

The CHANGELOG text mentions T-051 (profile telemetry) and numerous historical items; these are narrative only and do not change canonical threat entries. No threat-model update appears required from these units alone.
